Tranquil

/TRANG-kwil/ - the stress falls on TRANG · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Tranquil means calm.

The valley is at its most tranquil under new snow, every sound wrapped in white.

Worked Example

The pottery studio stays tranquil on Sunday mornings—wheels humming low, tea steaming on the sill, nobody in a hurry to speak.

Tranquil paints the scene, not just the mood: a tranquil harbor, a tranquil evening, a tranquil stretch of years. It promises freedom from disturbance—quieter than 'peaceful' and more outward than serene, which lives behind a person's eyes.

How Tranquil Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

peaceful

peaceful: free of conflict and disturbance, the broad everyday word

restful

restful: actively restores you, the way sleep does

Antonyms

hectic

hectic: crowded with rushed activity

noisy

noisy: filled with unwanted sound

How Strong Is It? — peaceful → tranquil → still

peaceful vs. tranquil

peaceful vs. tranquil: Peaceful is the milder, broader word—a peaceful afternoon may still hold lawnmowers and laughter.

still vs. tranquil

still vs. tranquil: Still goes further than peaceful or tranquil—stillness is the total pause, not a leaf turning, while a tranquil scene may yet ripple softly at its edges.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — tranquil

Root — tranquil: calm, still (Latin tranquillus)

Put it together

Put it together: Tranquil came over whole from Latin tranquillus, 'calm, still.' Scholars suspect trans- ('across, beyond') fused with a cousin of quies ('quiet')—'quiet through and through'—but the seams vanished in Roman times, so the word is best worn unpeeled.

Use the root in a new word: tranquilizer

Use the root in a new word: tranquilizer: Medicine kept the root busy: a tranquilizer is the vet's dart that turns a panicked, thrashing animal calm enough to treat.

Word Choice

neutral / descriptive

Tranquil is the scene-setter of this unit's calm family: places, hours, and stretches of life are tranquil. Serene belongs to faces and spirits; placid to temperaments and to surfaces that don't stir. If you only mean 'not noisy,' quiet is enough—tranquil promises that nothing is wrong beneath the hush.
